title: Add timing and response checks
learningGoal: Avoid sending reminders to people who have already engaged.

items.title: Insert a Wait Action
items.description: Add Wait after the first email. Start with 1 day as a training example, not a universal best timing rule.

items.title: Timing Is Context-Dependent
items.description: The right wait time depends on your audience, offer, and industry. Test and adjust.

items.title: Add Response Checks
items.description: Before any reminder, add a decision or exit mechanism that checks whether the contact has replied or booked.

items.title: Review Available Conditions
items.description: Check your account's available workflow conditions and appointment settings.

items.title: End the Path if Engaged
items.description: If the contact replied or booked, end the sales reminder path or remove them from the follow-up workflow.

items.title: Subject: Would a short call be useful?
items.description: Hi {{contact.first_name}}, Just following up on your enquiry. If a short conversation would help you decide on the next step, here is my calendar: [Insert booking link]. No pressure if the timing is not right. You can also reply with a question. Best, [Your name]

items.title: Send Only One Reminder
items.description: Send one helpful reminder, then end the workflow. A separate Customer Booked Appointment workflow can handle confirmations.

items.title: Wait Does Not Auto-Stop
items.description: A simple 1-day Wait does not automatically stop messages when someone books. Configure this logic explicitly.

items.title: SMS Requires Consent
items.description: Do not use SMS without suitable consent, registration, and compliance checks.

items.title: Exercise for Trainers
items.description: Describe two cases when a person should NOT receive the reminder.

keyPoint: A Wait action does not automatically know when someone has booked. You must explicitly configure reply checks, booking checks, or removal logic before sending any reminder.

actionSteps.title: Add a Wait action
actionSteps.description: Insert a 1-day Wait after the first email in your workflow.

actionSteps.title: Add response or booking checks
actionSteps.description: Configure conditions to check if the contact has replied or booked before sending a reminder.

actionSteps.title: Draft one reminder email
actionSteps.description: Write a single helpful reminder that ends the workflow after sending.

quizzes.question: Does a fixed Wait action automatically know when someone has booked an appointment?

options.option_text: Yes, Wait automatically stops when a booking is detected
No; you must configure booking or reply checks explicitly
Only if the calendar is integrated with LeadProspectrr
Yes, but only for appointments booked through the workflow link

quizzes.explanation: A simple Wait action does not automatically stop messages when someone books. You must explicitly configure reply checks, booking checks, or removal logic in the workflow.

quizzes.question: What are two valid reasons to stop a follow-up reminder?

options.option_text: The contact opened the email and clicked a link
The contact replied or booked an appointment

quizzes.explanation: If a contact has replied to your email or booked an appointment, they have engaged and should not receive a sales reminder. Other actions like opening an email or visiting a website do not necessarily indicate engagement.

quizzes.question: How many reminder emails should the workflow send?

options.option_text: One helpful reminder, then end the workflow
Two reminders: one at 1 day and one at 3 days

quizzes.explanation: Send one helpful reminder, then end the workflow. A separate Customer Booked Appointment workflow can handle confirmations and reminders for appointments.
